updates.title: IBM combines chat, decisions, and speech in Granite-Switch-4.1
updates.whatChanged: IBM released Granite-Switch-4.1-8B and Granite-Switch-4.1-30B on 15 October. Each model combines a general decision adapter, a safety-focused Guardian adapter, and Granite-Speech-5.0-Turbo-CTC for transcription. IBM says these components use about the same GPU VRAM as the base model and can share its KV cache.
updates.whyCare: You can serve chat, speech transcription, and specialized decisions through one model endpoint, without routing each task to a separate model. Shared KV-cache use may reduce extra GPU memory. Compare this setup with separate specialist models.
updates.before: Teams could compose task-specific adapters from Granite Libraries or route chat, classification, and speech tasks to separate models. The preconfigured Granite Switch combination was unavailable.
updates.after: Teams can run Granite Switch 4.1 in 8B or 30B sizes for chat, decisions, and transcription through one endpoint. The project supports vLLM through a plugin and native inference in llama.cpp.
updates.learn: Compare Granite Switch with separately deployed ASR and decision models for task accuracy, latency, throughput, and GPU memory. Verify adapter and shared-cache behavior in your serving runtime before consolidating endpoints.

sources.name: IBM Granite on Hugging Face - Granite Switch 4.1: Chat, Decisions, and Speech from One Endpoint

updates.architectureImplication: A multi-adapter model could consolidate separate endpoints for text, classification, and ASR, reducing serving duplication. Keep task-level evaluations and fallback routes because this release does not establish equal quality or reliability across tasks.
